chunks: Thereupon, Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said: If you are speaking a lie, may Allāh afflict you with white spots (leucoderma) which even the turban may not cover.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the curse of white spots in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This conditional curse (du'a bi'l-l'inn) reflects the high authority of the Imam’s speech, where his word becomes a decisive sign of truth or falsehood, a concept central to Shia theology regarding the infallible Imams. The specific affliction of leucoderma (birsa'), rendered so conspicuous that the turban cannot conceal it, serves as a public, visible seal of divine verification, linking physical manifestation to spiritual truth. This incident underscores the dynamic interplay between the Imam’s knowledge and the external validation of his statements in the early Islamic community.
